rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes the phrase as a circumstantial construction meaning an indicated object, like Hūd 11:72; alternatively, تلك may be a relative pronoun linked to بيمينك.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ( تلك بيمينك ) كقوله : { وهاذا بعلى شيخا } ( هود : 72 ) في انتصاب الحال بمعنى الإشارة ويجوز

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the question as asking what object is in Moses’ right hand.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه وما التي بيمينك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses the phrase as asking what this thing in Moses’ right hand is.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : معناه ما هذه التي في يمينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the staff and its benefits suggests a heart occupied by created things; Razi contrasts this with Muhammad’s undistracted vision of Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: فذكر العصا ومن كان قلبه مشغولا بالعصا ومنافعها كيف يكون مستغرقا في بحر معرفة الحق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Razi cites Muhammad’s response to being asked to praise God: he cannot enumerate the praise, and God is as He praised Himself; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ولكن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم عرض عليه الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff becoming a serpent teaches that attention to anything besides God is a distracting danger, like a lethal serpent; Razi links this to Abraham’s disavowal of false gods.
rows.anchor: ليعرف أن كل ما سوى الله فالالتفات إليه شاغل وهو كالحية المهلكة لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi cites a hadith that unpaid zakat wealth will come on Judgment Day in the form of a bald serpent; he gives no chain or grading.
rows.anchor: يجاء يوم القيامة بصاحب المال الذي لم يؤد زكاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had already answered by identifying the staff, but listed more uses as a means to prolong his conversation with God, which he loved.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه قال هي عصاي فقد تم الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اتوكأ means to lean on the staff when tired, pausing by the flock, or crossing a leap; التوكي and الاتكاء are compared with التوقي and الاتقاء.
rows.anchor: والتوكي ، والإتكاء ، واحد كالتوقي ، والإتقاء معناه اعتمد عليها إذا عييت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi contrasts Moses leaning on a staff with Muhammad relying on God’s mercy, citing divine sufficiency and protection for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( اتكىء على رحمتي ) بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 8:64, ومن اتبعك is coordinated with the pronoun in حسبك الله, so the meaning is that God suffices both Muhammad and the believers who follow him.
rows.anchor: معطوف على الكاف في قوله : { حسبك الله } والمعنى الله حسبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses shakes or strikes tree branches with the staff so leaves fall for his sheep to eat.
rows.anchor: أي أخبط بها فأضرب أغصان الشجر ليسقط ورقها على غنمي فتأكله

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes the verb’s vowel in expressions for shaking sheep, striking a man, and bread crumbling.
rows.anchor: هش الرغيف يهش بكسر الهاء . قاله ثعلب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reads وأهس with an unpointed sīn; Razi explains this form as driving or shooing sheep.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة : ( وأهس ) بالسين غير المنقوطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses mentions his own needs before the flock, his dependents; Razi contrasts this with Muhammad’s concern for his community in life and at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: غنمه رعيته فبدأ بمصالح نفسه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Razi cites Muhammad praying, “O God, guide my people, for they do not know”; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: اللهم اهد قومي فإنهم لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Razi says Muhammad will put his community first at the Resurrection, saying “My community, my community”; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يشتغل في الدنيا إلا بإصلاح أمر الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مآرب means needs or benefits; its singular is مأربة, with the rāʾ read in more than one way.
rows.anchor: أي حوائج ومنافع واحدتها مأربة بفتح الراء وضمها

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي وقطرب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Quṭrub also report مأربة with kasra; الأرب and الإربة likewise mean a need.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن الأعرابي وقطرب بكسر الراء أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخرى is feminine because مآرب conveys a collective group; أخر would also be correct, as in 2:184.
rows.anchor: لأن المآرب في معنى جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses states what he knows about the staff’s uses and summarizes the other, as yet unknown, purposes because God’s question signals hidden significance.
rows.anchor: عرف أن لله فيه أسرارا عظيمة فذكر ما عرف وعبر عن البواقي التي ما عرفها إجمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses presents the staff as ordinary, yet recognizes that God’s asking about it means it has further benefits, including occasioning God’s speech to him.
rows.anchor: إلهي ما هذه العصا إلا كغيرها ، لكنك لما سألت عنها عرفت أن لي فيها مآرب أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses generalizes about other uses in hope that God will ask about them, allowing their conversation to continue.
rows.anchor: أجمل رجاء أن يسأل ربه عن تلك المآرب فيسمع كلام الله مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By divine gentleness Moses began speaking, then awe overwhelmed and confused him, so he again gave a general answer.
rows.anchor: بسبب اللطف انطلق لسانه ثم غلبته الدهشة فانقطع لسانه وتشوش فكره

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb describes the staff as forked like a crook: it hooked or twisted branches, carried Moses’ gear, and could be planted with his cloak to make shade.
rows.anchor: ثم قال وهب : كانت ذات شعبتين كالمحجن ، فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unassigned report gives the staff further marvels: it lengthened into a bucket for drawing water, lit nights, fought enemies, bore fruit and supplies, produced water, and warded off vermin.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان فيها من المعجزات أنه كان يستقي بها فتطول بطول البئر وتصير شعبتاها دلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ mention of other uses prompts God to reveal a further, greater use of the staff that Moses had not recognized: its transformation into a serpent.
rows.anchor: أراد الله أن يعرفه أن فيها مأربة أخرى لا يفطن لها ولا يعرفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sandals signify flight and the staff pursuit: first removing the sandals, then casting the staff, symbolizes abandoning both escape and seeking to become wholly devoted to God.
rows.anchor: الرجل آلة الهرب واليد آلة الطلب فقال أولا : { فاخلع نعليك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even eminent Moses had to put aside his only two possessions, sandals and staff, before approaching God; a sinner burdened with a thousand loads of sin should consider how to approach.
rows.anchor: لما وصل إلى الحضرة ولم يكن معه إلا النعلان والعصا أمره بالقائهما حتى أمكنه الوصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad, detached from all, received everything, while Moses’ attachment to the staff led God to command him to cast it away.
rows.anchor: أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم كان مجردا عن الكل ما زاغ البصر فلا جرم وجد الكل

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbī uses the command to cast the staff to argue that capacity precedes the act: capacity must arrive while it is in Moses’ hand, since casting something no longer held is impossible.
rows.anchor: الكعبي تمسك به في أن الاستطاعة قبل الفعل فقال : القدرة على إلقاء العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The serpent is a compelling sign of Moses’ own prophethood: the earlier voice might have come from an angel or jinn and therefore did not establish it decisively.
rows.anchor: قلبها حية لتكون معجزة لموسى عليه السلام يعرف بها نبوة نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حَيّة is a general term covering male or female snakes, small or large; ثعبان denotes a great snake, while جان denotes a slender one.
rows.anchor: أما الحية فاسم جنس يقع على الذكر والأنثى والصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reconciliation is that the snake first appeared small and slender as a جان, then swelled into a large ثعبان.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت وقت انقلابها حية صغيرة دقيقة ثم تورمت وتزايد جرمها حتى صارت ثعبانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reconciliation is that it had the size of a ثعبان and the speed of a جان, supported by the description in 27:10.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت في شخص الثعبان وسرعة حركة الجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi describes the serpent as horse-maned, with jaws forty cubits apart, swallowing rocks and trees so that Moses heard stones crack inside it.
rows.anchor: كان لها عرف كعرف الفرس وكان بين لحييها أربعون ذراعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ fear can be explained as an instinctive reaction: he had never seen such a creature, and extreme panic can overwhelm rational knowledge.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك الخوف كان من نفرة الطبع لأنه عليه السلام ما شاهد مثل ذلك قط

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم الأنصاري
rows.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Anṣārī calls Moses’ fear strong evidence of his truthful prophethood, since a sorcerer knows his display is illusion and would not fear it.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو القاسم الأنصاري رحمه الله تعالى وذلك الخوف من أقوى الدلائل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Moses feared the serpent because he knew what Adam had suffered from it.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : خافها لأنه عليه السلام عرف ما لقي آدم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command do not fear alone does not prove Moses was afraid, as do not obey the disbelievers does not prove obedience; his turning and fleeing in 27:10 does prove fear, which Razi contrasts with Muhammad’s freedom from worldly attachment.
rows.anchor: مجرد قوله : { لا تخف } لا يدل على حصول الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses put his hand between the serpent’s teeth and it became wood; the verse’s future wording means he took it after it had become a serpent.
rows.anchor: روي أنه أدخل يده بين أسنانها فانقلبت خشبة والقرآن يدل عليه أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the serpent safely and its return to wood are further miracles, strengthening the proof beyond the staff’s first transformation.
rows.anchor: إدخال يده في فمها من غير ضرر معجزة وانقلابها خشبا معجز آخر فيكون فيه توالي المعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi regards the report that Moses took the serpent while still afraid as unlikely, since signs had accumulated and God had promised to restore it.
rows.anchor: روي مع الخوف ولكنه بعيد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view is that God’s command removed Moses’ fear and reassured him enough to take the serpent by its jaws.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم لما قال له ربه : { لا تخف } بلغ من ذلك ذهاب خوفه

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf derives سيرة from السير, like ركبة from الركوب, then explains how it extended to mean a way or manner.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : السيرة من السير كالركبة من الركوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing treats سيرتها as منصوب after an omitted preposition, meaning سنعيدها إلى سيرتها.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : بنزع الخافض يعني إلى سيرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, سنعيدها stands independently: God will make the serpent a staff again, with سيرتها the object of an implied تسير, restoring its former uses.
rows.anchor: أن يكون سنعيدها مستقلا بنفسه غير متعلق بسيرتها بمعنى أنها كانت أولا عصا فصارت حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The voice honored Moses; the additional miracle is a further grace whose succession can dispel the estrangement in his heart.
rows.anchor: ليكون توالي الخلع والكرامات سببا لزوال الوحشة عن قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Moses the serpent in advance so that he would not fear it when confronting Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: عند فرعون لا يخافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a poor shepherd appointed to a great mission, the transformation demonstrated that the God who could do this could also support him in establishing religion.
rows.anchor: كان راعيا فقيرا ثم إنه نصب للمنصب العظيم فلعله بقي في قلبه تعجب من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled from the very staff he had claimed and valued; Razi reads this as a lesson to flee toward God and say God alone, leaving created attachments.
rows.anchor: ادعيت أنها عصاك وأن لك فيها مآرب أخرى فلم تفر منها

none: The segment contains only quoted Qur’anic text, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi resumes his earlier discussion of the benefits and conditions of supplication under 2:286 and adds points relevant to Moses’ prayer.
rows.anchor: أما البحث الأول : وهو فائدة الدعاء وشرائطه فقد تقدم في تفسير قوله : { ربنا لا تؤاخذنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest degree of perfection is to be perfect in oneself and to perfect others; God is eternally perfect in Himself but perfects others in time.
rows.anchor: للكمال مراتب ودرجات وأعلاها أن يكون كاملا في ذاته مكملا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although perfecting others is a perfection, its absence from eternity is no defect: perfecting means making something complete, and eternally making the already complete is impossible.
rows.anchor: التكميل عبارة عن جعل الشيء كاملا وذلك لا يتحقق إلا عند عدم الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that God would lack a perfection if He did not perfect eternally fails because eternal action is impossible; impossibilities such as making a self or counting endless motions do not imply incapacity.
rows.anchor: النقصان إنما يلزم لو كان ذلك ممكنا في الأزل لكنا بينا أن الفعل الأزلي محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings some possibilities into existence because nonexistents are infinite; bringing all into being would mean an infinite number entered existence.
rows.anchor: أن المعدومات غير متناهية فلو أجلس الكل على مائدة الوجود لدخل ما لا نهاية له في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God created all possibilities, He could create nothing afterward, since creating what already exists is impossible and this would turn ability into incapacity.
rows.anchor: أنه لو أوجد الكل لما بقي بعد ذلك قادرا على الإيجاد لأن إيجاد الموجود محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating everything would erase distinctions between the capable agent and what is naturally necessary; capacity is perfection, while natural necessity is deficiency.
rows.anchor: لو دخل الكل في الوجود لما بقي فيه تمييز فلا يتميز القادر على الموجب والقدرة كمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the finite number of existent things is a small banquet compared with infinitely many deprived nonexistents; selection either presupposes an unexplained entitlement or is purposeless.
rows.anchor: الموجودات متناهية والمعدومات غير متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection is framed as God giving and withholding neither from stinginess nor generosity, which would seem unworthy of the Most Generous.
rows.anchor: يعطي ويمنع لا بخلا ولا كرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that these doubts project human choices onto God; God is not questioned about what He does, while people are, as 21:23 states.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الشبهات إنما تدور في العقول والخيالات لأن الإنسان يحاول قياس فعله على فعلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal outpouring of existence from divine mercy is the general hospitality and comprehensive table meant by 7:156.
rows.anchor: هذا الوجود الفائض من نور رحمته على جميع الممكنات هو الضيافة العامة والمائدة الشاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals surpass inanimate things because they distinguish existence from nonexistence and use inanimate things as tools, whereas inanimates have no awareness of their own existence.
rows.anchor: الجماد لا خبر عنده من وجوده فوجوده بالنسبة إليه كالعدم وعدمه كالوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as mercy gave existence to some possibilities, it gives life to some existent things and leaves others inanimate; life is to inanimacy as light, sight, and existence are to their opposites.
rows.anchor: اقتضيا وضع مائدة الحياة لبعض الموجودات دون البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Living beings perceive pleasure and pain, good and evil, and therefore need power to pursue what benefits them and flee harm; without it they would remain helpless prey.
rows.anchor: احتجنا إلى طلب الملائم ودفع المنافي فإن لم تكن لنا قدرة على الهرب والطلب والدفع والجذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete mercy grants power to some living beings, just as it grants life to some existent things and existence to some nonexistents.
rows.anchor: فاقتضت الرحمة التامة تخصيص بعض الأحياء بالقدرة كما اقتضت تخصيص بعض الموجودات بالحياة

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: Razi cites a saying addressed to the intellect: through it God humiliates, rewards, and punishes; he uses this to frame reason as an honored gift, without giving a grading.
rows.anchor: بك أهين وبك أثيب وبك أعاقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants reason, insight, and guidance; existence, life, power, and reason are four gifts, with reason completing the set.
rows.anchor: فعند هذه الدرجة فازوا بالخلع الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the final Prophet is the best of the prophets and humans are the best bodily creatures, reason is best among the gifts because it comes last.
rows.anchor: الخاتم يجب أن يكون أفضل ألا ترى أن رسولنا صلى الله عليه وسلم لما كان خاتم النبيين كان أفضل الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason’s innate necessary truths are like shining stars: just as stars guide travelers through earthly darkness, these truths guide minds toward the spiritual world.
rows.anchor: العلوم الضرورية البديهية المركوزة في بدائه العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason sees the mark of createdness on its own knowledge and gifts, inferring an inscriber from the inscriptions and recognizing that maker and building differ from what is made.
rows.anchor: رأى رقم الحدوث على تلك الجواهر وعلى جميع تلك الخلع فاستدل بتلك الأرقام على راقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Confronted with the eternal world’s overwhelming light, reason becomes bewildered and turns to its source, asking for an expanded breast amid deep seas, layered darkness, and inner and outer enemies.
rows.anchor: غلبته دهشة أنوار الأزلية فعميت عيناه فبقي متحيرا فالتجأ بطبعه إلى مفيض الأنوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for an expanded breast because without divine help the gifts of existence, life, power, and reason could expose him to harm rather than lead to higher ranks.
rows.anchor: فإن لم تشرح لي صدري ولم تكن لي عونا في كل الأمور انقطعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No act occurs until the servant wills it, but a created will needs an agent; if the servant creates it, another will is needed endlessly, so God creates the will and truly facilitates affairs.
rows.anchor: فهذه الإرادة صفة محدثة ولا بد لها من فاعل وفاعلها إن كان هو العبد افتقر في تحصيل تلك الإرادة إلى إرادة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expanding the breast expresses the recipient’s readiness and facilitating the affair expresses the agent’s efficacy; God grants both, so the two prayers argue that all events occur by His decree, wisdom, and power.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن حصول الفاعل بقوله : { ويسر لى أمرى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that Moses asks not only for an open breast but also for the actual execution of his mission and attainment of its goal.
rows.anchor: كأن موسى عليه السلام قال : إلهي لا أكتفي بشرح الصدر ولكن أطلب منك تنفيذ الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading pairs God’s four gifts of existence, life, power, and reason with four services in prayer: standing, recitation, bowing, and prostration.
rows.anchor: وأقم الصلاة لذكري فإن فيها أنواعا أربعة من الخدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading treats prophethood as a fifth gift and the prophetic mission as its corresponding service; Moses asks for help because of his weakness, limited means, and powerful opponent.
rows.anchor: لما أعطاه الخلعة الخامسة وهي خلعة الرسالة قال : { رب اشرح لى صدرى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplication is a means of nearness to God, and Moses prayed here seeking that nearness; Razi says he will establish that prayer brings closeness and that Moses sought it.
rows.anchor: الدعاء سبب القرب من الله تعالى وإنما اشتغل موسى بهذا الدعاء طلبا للقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi points to Qur’anic question-and-answer passages on theological matters: the crescents, the spirit, the mountains, and the Hour.
rows.anchor: ذكر السؤال والجواب في كتابه في عدة مواضع منها أصولية ومنها فروعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also notes six successive legal questions in al-Baqara, beginning with what people should spend and the answer naming parents and relatives.
rows.anchor: أحدها : { يسئلونك ماذا ينفقون قل ما أنفقتم من خير فللوالدين
